result.title: Cycle WAM: Coupling Action and Video through Cycle Consistency
result.summary: Recent advances in video modeling have driven substantial progress in world action models (WAMs). Existing approaches exploit pretrained video priors by decoding actions from latent representations or inferring them from generated videos. The underlying link is causal: robot actions produce changes in the scene, and video observations of these changes provide evidence for inferring the actions that produced them. However, existing training formulations do not by themselves ensure that actions and their predicted visual consequences are consistent, potentially limiting the use of pretrained capabilities. We treat video and action as paired modalities linked by this causal relationship and learn their correspondence through a unified training framework designed to better exploit pretrained video priors. Cycle WAM first augments video-action co-training with bidirectional conversion to reinforce cross-modal correspondence and recover forward and inverse dynamics. It then introduces a differentiable cycle-reconstruction objective to further couple the two mappings. The resulting model supports both forward and inverse dynamics, with the potential to improve performance through more effective use of pretrained video priors. Cycle WAM achieves state-of-the-art performance among comparable methods on LIBERO-Pro and substantially improves DreamZero on DROID. Comparisons with UWM characterize its inverse-dynamics performance and show sharper visual detail in the displayed forward-dynamics predictions.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 Cycle WAM，将视频与动作视为因果配对模态，在视频-动作联合训练中加入双向转换，并引入可微的循环重建目标来耦合前向与逆向动力学，从而更充分地利用预训练视频先验；在 LIBERO-Pro 与 DROID 上报告了相应提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其循环一致性监督可能可供核查：用「动作→视觉后果→动作」的可重建性约束内部表示，或可用于检验 latent 状态是否真正保留任务必要视觉信息、而非旁路坍缩。
